newsitem.title: CANADA: Tropical Storm Hortense rakes Canada's maritimes.
newsitem.headline: Tropical Storm Hortense rakes Canada's maritimes.

text.p: Hortense, once a fierce hurricane with 140 mph (225 kph) winds, was downgraded to a post-tropical storm on Sunday after pounding Canada's maritime provinces with large ocean swells and heavy rain.
Hortense was losing its characteristics and fading fast over the cooler waters of the north Atlantic, Canadian weather forecasters said.
At 2 p.m. EDT (1800 GMT), the centre of Hortense was located at latitude 46.6 north, longitude 54.6 west, about 250 miles (400 km) west-southwest of St. John's, Newfoundland.

Maximum winds were 50 mph (80 kph) and were expected to weaken to 40 mph (65 kph) this evening when Hortense passes near southern Newfoundland, said Glenda Saulnier, a meteorologist with Environment Canada.
Hortense is expected to be at latitude 46.5 north, longitude 50.6 west by 8 p.m. EDT (2400 GMT), she said.
"It's essentially a low pressure system. The only thing that differentiates it from a regular storm is that there is a lot more rain," Saulnier said.
Forecasters said Hortense, born in the Atlantic east of the Lesser Antilles, would die gradually over the next day and no further advisories would be issued.

Earlier in the week the hurricane dumped up to two feet (0.6 meters) of rain on Puerto Rico and the Dominican Republic. Dominican officials put the number of dead as high as 10, with 50 people missing, and 16 people were killed in Puerto Rico.
